readings.subsection: The Inner Court and Temple Proper
readings.title: The Place of Slaughter
readings.subtitle: Rooms and tables for preparing the offerings.
readings.text: [Ezekiel 40:38] And there was a room with its entrance by the posts of the gate, where they washed <dn>את</dn> the ascending offering. [39] And in the porch of the gate were two tables on this side and two tables on that side, on which to slay <dn>את</dn> the ascending offering, and <dn>את</dn> the sin offering, and <dn>את</dn> the guilt offering. [40] And on the outer side, as one went up to the entrance of the north gate, were two tables. And on the other side of the porch of the gate were two tables. [41] Four tables were on this side and four tables on that side, by the side of the gate, eight tables on which they slew. [42] And there were four tables of hewn stone for the ascending offering, one cubit and a half long, one cubit and a half wide, and one cubit high. On these they placed <dn>את</dn> the instruments with which they slew <dn>את</dn> the ascending offering and the slaughterings. [43] And the double hooks, a handbreadth wide, were fastened all around. And on the tables was the flesh of the offerings.

readings.subsection: The Inner Court and Temple Proper
readings.title: The Priests' Chambers
readings.subtitle: Rooms for the singers and the sons of Tsaḏoq.
readings.text: [Ezekiel 40:44] And on the outside of the inner gate were the rooms for the singers in the inner courtyard, one at the side of the north gate and facing south, and the other at the side of the south gate facing north. [45] And <dn>he</dn> said to me, <dq>“This room facing south is for the priests who guard <dn>את</dn> the duty of the House.</dq> [46] <dq>“And the room facing north is for the priests who guard <dn>את</dn> the duty of the slaughter-place, they are the sons of Tsaḏoq, from the sons of Lěvi, who come near <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to serve <dn>Him</dn>.”</dq> [47] And <dn>he</dn> measured <dn>את</dn> the courtyard, one hundred cubits long and one hundred cubits wide, a square. And the slaughter-place was in front of the House.

readings.subsection: The Inner Court and Temple Proper
readings.title: The Temple Proper
readings.subtitle: Measurements of the Porch, the Hěḵal, and the Most Set-apart Place.
readings.text: [Ezekiel 40:48] And <dn>he</dn> brought me to the porch of the House and measured <dn>את</dn> the doorposts of the porch, five cubits on this side and five cubits on that side. And the width of the gate was three cubits on this side and three cubits on that side. [49] The length of the porch was twenty cubits, and the width eleven cubits. And by the steps which led up to it there were columns by the doorposts, one on this side and one on that side. [Ezekiel 41:1] And <dn>he</dn> brought me into the Hěḵal, and <dn>he</dn> measured <dn>את</dn> the doorposts, six cubits wide on one side and six cubits wide on the other side, the width of the Tent. [2] And the entrance was ten cubits wide, and the side walls of the entrance were five cubits on this side and five cubits on the other side. And <dn>he</dn> measured its length, forty cubits, and twenty cubits wide. [3] And <dn>he</dn> went inside and measured <dn>את</dn> the doorposts, two cubits, and the entrance six cubits high, and the width of the entrance seven cubits. [4] And <dn>he</dn> measured the length, twenty cubits, and the width twenty cubits, to the front of the Hěḵal. And <dn>he</dn> said to me, <dq>“This is the Most Set-apart Place.”</dq>

readings.subsection: The Inner Court and Temple Proper
readings.title: The Side Rooms of the House
readings.subtitle: A three-level structure with winding passages.
readings.text: [Ezekiel 41:5] And <dn>he</dn> measured <dn>את</dn> the wall of the House, six cubits, and the width of each side room all around the House was four cubits on every side. [6] And the side rooms were on three levels, one above the other, thirty rooms on each level, they rested on ledges which were for the side rooms all around, to be supported, but not fastened to the wall of the House. [7] And there was a broadening and a winding upwards for the side rooms, for the winding around the House went up like steps. And the width of the structure increased as one went up from the lowest level to the highest by way of the middle one. [8] And <dn>I</dn> saw <dn>את</dn> the height all around the House: the foundation of the side rooms, a rod’s length of six cubits. [9] The thickness of the outer wall of the side rooms was five cubits, and that which was left between the side rooms of the House [10] and the rooms was a width of twenty cubits all around the House on every side. [11] And the door of the side room was toward the open space, one door toward the north and another toward the south. And the width of the place of the open space was five cubits all around.

readings.subsection: The Inner Court and Temple Proper
readings.title: Overall Temple Dimensions
readings.subtitle: The western building and the total length of the complex.
readings.text: [Ezekiel 41:12] And the building that was in front of the separate place at the side toward the west was seventy cubits wide, and the wall of the building was five cubits thick all around, and its length ninety cubits. [13] Then <dn>he</dn> measured <dn>את</dn> the House, one hundred cubits long. And the separate place with <dn>את</dn> the building and its walls, were one hundred cubits long, [14] and the width of the front of the House, and of the separate place eastward, was one hundred cubits. [15] And <dn>he</dn> measured <dn>את</dn> the length of the building to the front of the separate place behind it, and its galleries on the one side and on the other side, one hundred cubits, as well as the inner Hěḵal and the porches of the courtyard. [16] The doorposts and the narrowed window frames, and the galleries all around, their three levels opposite the threshold, were panelled with wood. From the ground to the windows, and the windows were covered, [17] from the space above the door, even to the inner house, as well as outside, and on every wall all around, inside and outside, by measure.

readings.subsection: The Inner Court and Temple Proper
readings.title: Temple Adornments
readings.subtitle: Carvings of keruḇim, palm trees, and the wooden altar.
readings.text: [Ezekiel 41:18] And it was made with keruḇim and palm trees, and a palm tree between keruḇ and keruḇ. A keruḇ had two faces, [19] so that the face of a man was toward a palm tree on one side, and the face of a young lion toward a palm tree on the other side – made on all the House all around. [20] From the floor to the space above the door, and on the wall of the Hěḵal, keruḇim and palm trees were carved. [21] The doorposts of the Hěḵal were square, and the front of the set-apart place, the appearance of one was like the appearance of the other. [22] The slaughter-place was of wood, three cubits high, and its length two cubits. And its corners, and its length, and its sides were of wood. And <dn>he</dn> said to me, <dq>“This is the table that is before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”</dq> [23] And the Hěḵal and the set-apart place had two doors. [24] And each of the doors had two panels, two folding panels, two panels for one door and two panels for the other door. [25] And keruḇim and palm trees were carved on the doors of the Hěḵal, like those carved on the walls. And thick wood was on the front of the porch outside. [26] And narrowed window frames and palm trees were on one side and on the other, on the sides of the porch, and on the side rooms of the House, and thick wood.

readings.subsection: The Priests' Quarters and Outer Complex
readings.title: The Set-Apart Rooms for the Priests
readings.subtitle: Chambers for eating the most set-apart offerings and storing garments.
readings.text: [Ezekiel 42:1] And <dn>he</dn> brought me out into the outer courtyard, the way toward the north. And <dn>he</dn> brought me into the room which was opposite the separate place, and which was opposite the building to the north. [2] Along the length which was one hundred cubits, was the north door, the width was fifty cubits. [3] Opposite the inner courtyard of twenty cubits, and opposite the pavement of the outer courtyard, gallery against gallery in three levels. [4] And before the rooms, toward the inside, was a walk ten cubits wide, a way of one cubit. And their doors were to the north. [5] And the upper rooms were shorter, because the galleries took away space from them more than from the lower and middle levels of the building. [6] For they were in three levels and had no columns like the columns of the courtyards, so the upper level was set back more than the lower and middle levels from the ground up. [7] As for the outer wall by the side of the rooms, toward the outer courtyard facing the rooms, its length was fifty cubits. [8] For the length of the rooms toward the outer courtyard was fifty cubits, and that facing the Hěḵal was one hundred cubits. [9] And below these rooms was the entrance on the east side, as one enters them from the outer courtyard. [10] In the thickness of the wall of the courtyard toward the east, opposite the separate place and opposite the building, were rooms. [11] And the way in front of them was like the appearance of the rooms which were toward the north, as long and as wide as the others, and all their exits and entrances were according to plan. [12] And according to the doors of the rooms that were toward the south, there was a door in front of the way, the way in front of the wall toward the east, as one enters them. [13] And <dn>he</dn> said to me, <dq>“The north rooms and the south rooms, which are opposite the separate place, are the set-apart rooms where the priests who approach <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> eat <dn>את</dn> the most set-apart offerings. There they place <dn>את</dn> the most set-apart items, and <dn>את</dn> the grain offering, and <dn>את</dn> the sin offering, and <dn>את</dn> the guilt offering, for the place is set-apart.</dq> [14] <dq>“When the priests enter, they are not to go out of the set-apart room into the outer courtyard, but leave their garments in which they attend there, for they are set-apart, and shall put on other garments and shall draw near to that which is for the people.”</dq>

readings.subsection: The Priests' Quarters and Outer Complex
readings.title: Measuring the Outer Wall
readings.subtitle: A wall to separate the set-apart from the common.
readings.text: [Ezekiel 42:15] And when <dn>he</dn> had ended measuring <dn>את</dn> the inner House, <dn>he</dn> brought me out through the gate that faces east, and measured it all around. [16] <dn>He</dn> measured <dn>את</dn> the east side with the measuring rod, five hundred rods by the measuring rod all around. [17] <dn>He</dn> measured <dn>את</dn> the north side, five hundred rods by the measuring rod all around. [18] <dn>He</dn> measured <dn>את</dn> the south side, five hundred rods by the measuring rod. [19] <dn>He</dn> turned round to the west side and measured five hundred rods by the measuring rod. [20] On the four sides <dn>he</dn> measured it. It had a wall all around, five hundred long and five hundred wide, to separate the set-apart places from the common.

readings.title: The Esteem of YeHoVaH Returns
readings.subtitle: The House is filled with His presence and declared His eternal throne.
readings.text: [Ezekiel 43:1] And <dn>he</dn> led me to the gate, the gate facing east. [2] And see, the esteem of the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl came from the way of the east. And <dn>His</dn> voice was like the sound of many waters, and the earth shone from <dn>His</dn> esteem. [3] And it was like the appearance of the vision which <dn>I</dn> saw, like the vision which <dn>I</dn> saw when <dn>He</dn> came to destroy the city. And the visions were like the vision which <dn>I</dn> saw by the River Keḇar, and <dn>I</dn> fell on <dn>my</dn> face. [4] And the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came into the House by way of the gate facing east. [5] And the Spirit took me up and brought me into the inner courtyard. And see, the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> filled the House. [6] And <dn>I</dn> heard someone speaking to me from the House, while a man stood beside me. [7] And <dn>He</dn> said to me, <dq>“Son of man, this is <dn>את</dn> the place of <dn>My</dn> throne and <dn>את</dn> the place of the soles of <dn>My</dn> feet, when <dn>I</dn> dwell in the midst of the children of Yisra’ěl forever, and the house of Yisra’ěl shall no longer defile <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> set-apart Name, they nor their sovereigns, by their whoring and by the corpses of their sovereigns on their high places.</dq> [8] <dq>“When they placed their threshold by <dn>My</dn> threshold, and their doorpost by <dn>My</dn> doorpost, with a wall between them and <dn>Me</dn>, they defiled <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> set-apart Name by the abominations which they have done. So <dn>I</dn> consumed them in <dn>My</dn> displeasure.</dq> [9] <dq>“Now let them put their whoring and the corpses of their sovereigns far away from <dn>Me</dn>, and <dn>I</dn> shall dwell in their midst forever.</dq> [10] <dq>“Son of man, explain <dn>את</dn> the House to the house of Yisra’ěl, and when they are ashamed of their crookednesses, they shall measure <dn>את</dn> the measurements.</dq> [11] <dq>“And since they shall be ashamed of all that they did, make known to them <dn>את</dn> the design of the House and its structure, and its exits and its entrances, its entire design and all its laws, and all its forms and all its Torot. And write it down before their eyes, so that they observe its entire design and all its laws, and shall do them.</dq> [12] <dq>“This is the Torah of the House: Upon the mountaintop, all the boundary of it, all around, is most set-apart. See, this is the Torah of the House.</dq>

readings.title: The Slaughter-Place and Its Consecration
readings.subtitle: The measurements and the seven-day ceremony for the altar.
readings.text: [Ezekiel 43:13] “And these are the measurements of the slaughter-place in cubits, that cubit being one cubit and a handbreadth, and the base one cubit high and one cubit wide, with a rim all around its edge of one span. And this is the upper part of the slaughter-place. [14] “And from the base on the ground to the lower ledge, two cubits, and the width of the ledge one cubit, and from the smaller ledge to the larger ledge four cubits, and the width of the ledge one cubit. [15] “And the slaughter-place hearth is four cubits high, and four horns extending upward from the hearth. [16] “And the slaughter-place hearth is twelve cubits long, and twelve wide, square at its four corners. [17] “And the ledge is fourteen long and fourteen wide on its four sides, with a rim of half a cubit around it, and its base one cubit all around, and its steps face east.” [18] And <dn>He</dn> said to me, <dq>“Son of man, thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘These are the laws for the slaughter-place on the day when it is made, for offering ascending offerings on it, and for sprinkling blood on it.</dq> [19] <dq>And you shall give <dn>את</dn> a young bull for a sin offering to the priests, the Lěvites, who are of the seed of Tsaḏoq, who approach unto <dn>Me</dn>,’ declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [20] <dq>And you shall take some of its blood and put it on the four horns of the slaughter-place, on the four corners of the ledge, and on the rim around it, and shall cleanse it and make atonement for it.</dq> [21] <dq>And you shall take <dn>את</dn> the bull of the sin offering, and shall burn it in the appointed place of the House, outside the set-apart place.</dq> [22] <dq>And on the second day you bring <dn>את</dn> a male goat, a perfect one, for a sin offering. And they shall cleanse <dn>את</dn> the slaughter-place, as they cleansed it with the bull.</dq> [23] <dq>When you have ended cleansing it, bring <dn>את</dn> a young bull, a perfect one, and a ram from the flock, a perfect one.</dq> [24] <dq>And you shall bring them before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and the priests shall throw salt on them and offer them up as an ascending offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [25] <dq>Prepare <dn>את</dn> a goat for a sin offering daily for seven days, and prepare <dn>את</dn> a young bull and a ram from the flock, perfect ones.</dq> [26] <dq>For seven days they shall make atonement for the slaughter-place and cleanse it, and ordain it.</dq> [27] <dq>And when these days are completed it shall be, on the eighth day and thereafter, that the priests make <dn>את</dn> your ascending offerings and your peace offerings on the slaughter-place, and <dn>I</dn> shall accept you,’ declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”</dq>
